candidate.architecture: native C++ runtime on ggml with CPU/CUDA/HIP-ROCm/Vulkan/Metal backends and GGUF-oriented model packaging

released_voice_relevant_surface: Qwen3-ASR-0.6B and 1.7B: German listed; GGUF 16/Q8; Stream
Qwen3-TTS 0.6B/1.7B variants: German listed; GGUF 16/Q8; not marked Stream in v0.7.0 table
source_observations.release_scope: v0.7.0 reports 62 model families and 85+ variants and provides a common native framework plus comparison/Arena tooling.
source_observations.performance_boundary: Upstream reports substantial speed/VRAM gains on selected model paths, but these are upstream measurements and grant zero Frankenstein latency, residency, German-quality or acceptance credit.

comparison_to_existing_trigger7_runtime_.CrispASR: audio.cpp is broader: it exposes several ASR, TTS and VAD families behind one native framework rather than serving only as the already-audited Qwen-oriented consolidated C++/GGUF challenger. The prior CrispASR source audit already falsified the stronger assumption that one process implies one shared simultaneously resident ASR/TTS model instance; audio.cpp receives no such memory-sharing assumption.
comparison_to_existing_trigger7_runtime_.NeMo-Speech.cpp: audio.cpp is a useful counter-runtime because its released surface directly includes Qwen3-ASR plus multiple German TTS candidates, while NeMo-Speech.cpp remains the existing NVIDIA-native ASR/VAD/TTS substrate candidate. Source breadth alone does not establish lower jitter, lower residency or better German quality.

important_negative_or_open_points: Qwen3-TTS is not marked Stream in the v0.7.0 support table, so audio.cpp v0.7.0 cannot be credited as a complete low-latency Qwen3-ASR+Qwen3-TTS Frankenstein voice path from source claims alone.
A shared runtime does not prove shared model weights, shared KV/cache memory, lower combined RSS/VRAM, or safe concurrent ASR+TTS execution.
Runtime Apache-2.0 does not override model-specific licenses or redistribution constraints.
No clay-direct-dev build, model download, hash verification, component benchmark, German corpus run or end-to-end voice run was executed by this audit.
hypothesis: If audio.cpp can host the German ASR/TTS candidates needed by Frankenstein with less framework duplication and lower concurrent resident/tail cost than the best NeMo-Speech.cpp/CrispASR paths while preserving the VoiceIntent/GWT/state/effect boundary, it may become the preferred low-level native speech substrate.
counterhypothesis: Model-specific runtimes remain superior; audio.cpp breadth adds integration convenience but no target p95/p99 or resident-resource benefit, or its current streaming gaps force a mixed runtime anyway.
